title: Architecture & Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance, ADRs
author: Avery Chen
content:
Summary
=======
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's cross-cutting architecture and engineering standards for API design, coding style, infrastructure-as-code, model-serving, observability, and performance. It also documents the ADR (Architecture Decision Record) process and links to representative ADRs. The goal is to provide a single reference for design reviews, onboarding, and audits so teams can build predictable, reliable, and performant inference services.

Scope & Audience
----------------
- Applies to all services and components that are customer-facing (Hosted API) and internal platform services (inference-gateway, model-store, routing-service, autoscaler).
- Intended audience: software engineers, ML engineers, platform engineers, and SREs.
- Exclusions: quick prototypes and PoCs must be explicitly recorded as exempt in the PR description.

Principles
----------
1. Production-first: design for predictable latency, correctness, and recoverability.
2. Observable by default: metrics, traces, and structured logs shipped with every service.
3. Infrastructure as code: no manual changes to production.
4. Backwards-compatibility: API and model contract changes must have migration plans or versioning.
5. Ownership: every service and standard has a documented owner and reviewer rotation.

1) API Standards
----------------
Purpose: keep our API predictable and easy to integrate with while allowing flexibility for evolving model capabilities.
Required practices:
- Use RESTful resource-based endpoints for platform services and WebSocket/HTTP streaming for token streaming. Example: GET /v1/models, POST /v1/engines/{engine_id}/completions.
- OpenAPI Spec required for all public and internal HTTP APIs; maintain spec in repo under /api/openapi/ and publish to the API registry.
- Versioning: path-based major versioning: /v1/, /v2/. Minor changes should be additive and non-breaking.
- Auth: JWT bearer tokens for public API; mTLS + service tokens for internal control-plane endpoints.
- Rate limiting: enforce per-key and per-route limits. Use headers X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset. Default burst policy: 100 req/min, adjustable per product.
- Errors: use RFC7807 problem+json for structured errors. Include fields: type, title, status, detail, instance, and optionally code. Example error body: {"type":"https://api.redwood.ai/errors/invalid-input","title":"Invalid input","status":400,"detail":"Prompt exceeds max_tokens","code":"PROMPT_TOO_LONG"}.
- Timeouts: frontend gateway 30s (configurable per route); model inference timeout documented per engine.
- Payload size: accept up to 1MB for requests; larger batch/streaming workloads must use chunked upload (S3 presigned) and reference the object.

API Checklist (pre-merge)
- OpenAPI spec present and CI-validated.
- Contract tests added (happy + error flows).
- Backwards-compatibility rationale or migration plan.

2) Coding Standards
-------------------
Languages and formatting:
- Go for high-throughput, low-latency services (inference-gateway, autoscaler). Python for orchestration and data pipelines. TypeScript for web console.
- Enforce formatting: gofmt/gci; black/isort for Python; prettier/eslint for TS.
- Linting: run golangci-lint, bandit (Python), and Snyk/ESLint for JS.

PR & Review Rules:
- Small PRs (<400 LOC preferred). Provide a short design rationale.
- At least 2 reviewers for production-impacting PRs (runtime, infra, security).
- Include unit tests and integration tests where applicable; >= 90% line coverage for critical modules.

Error handling and observability:
- Do not swallow errors. Wrap with contextual information. Use structured logging (JSON) with fields: timestamp, service, trace_id, span_id, level, message, err_code.
- Correlation IDs: accept X-Request-Id and attach trace_id to logs and spans.

3) Infrastructure Standards
--------------------------
IaC and environments:
- All infra must be defined in Terraform modules stored in infra/terraform. Use module registry and module version pinning.
- Environment separation: dev, staging, prod (separate accounts or projects). No cross-environment manual changes.
- Network: VPC per environment, private subnets for compute. Public-facing endpoints must sit behind the edge load balancer (edge-proxy).

Security & secrets:
- Secrets in KMS-backed secret manager (Cloud KMS/HSM). No plaintext secrets in repo.
- Service accounts: least privilege, and keys rotated every 90 days.

Images & CI/CD:
- Container images built in a reproducible build pipeline; base images scanned and pinned. Image tag policy: semantic: <service>-<git-sha>.
- CI: merge to main triggers pipeline that runs unit tests, static analysis, build image, run integration smoke, and deploy to canary.

4) Model-Serving Standards
-------------------------
Purpose: ensure models are served consistently, safely, and with measurable cost/latency characteristics.
Model artifacts & versioning:
- Store model artifacts in model-store with metadata: model_id, version, architecture, tokenizer_hash, quantization_profile, artifact_sha256.
- Semantic versioning for model changes (major = incompatible tokenizer or API changes).
- Quantization profiles stored alongside model (e.g. q8_optimized_v2).

Runtime contract:
- inference-gateway exposes consistent request shape: {"model_id":"rwd-small-v1","input":"...","max_tokens":128,"temperature":0.2}.
- KV cache semantics documented: per-session cache keyed by model_id+session_id; eviction policy LRU with TTL default 10m.

Batching & latency:
- Batched inference allowed for background/low-priority workloads. Real-time requests must be routed to low-latency pools.
- Batching window: default 10ms for latency-sensitive pools; configurable per pool.

Fallbacks & compatibility:
- Define fallback chains in model-routing policy: rwd-large-v2 -> rwd-medium-v2 -> rwd-small-v1. Fallbacks must preserve tokenization compatibility or include a conversion step.

Model Testing:
- Add model-specific unit tests and an eval suite (prompt-sets and benchmarks). Evaluate for accuracy regressions before rollout.

Example model metadata table (text):
- model_id | version | arch | quant_profile | owner | sLO_target
- rwd-small | v1 | transformer | q5_0 | ml-models | p95_latency <= 120ms

5) Observability Standards
-------------------------
Metrics (minimum):
- request_count (labels: service, route, model_id, outcome)
- request_latency_ms (p50,p90,p95,p99)
- error_count (by code)
- model_cache_hit_ratio
- batch_size_distribution

Tracing & Logs:
- Trace every external request through the stack; propagate W3C traceparent. Samples: 100% for canaries, 1% for prod by default with dynamic sampling on anomalies.
- Logs must be structured JSON and include trace_id, span_id, service, severity, and stable error_code.

Dashboards & Alerts:
- Maintain per-service dashboards: traffic, latency, errors, underlying infra (GPU utilization, memory).
- Alert rules (examples):
  - High error rate: error_count > 0.5% of requests for 5m -> P1 page.
  - SLO breach warning: p95_latency > SLO_threshold for 10m -> P2.
  - Model-serving GPU saturation: utilization > 85% for 15m -> P2.

6) Performance Standards (SLOs & SLIs)
------------------------------------
SLOs (example defaults):
- Hosted text-generation (small models): p95 latency <= 150ms, availability 99.9% monthly.
- Hosted chat/large models: p95 latency <= 1200ms, availability 99.5% monthly.
- Embeddings: p95 latency <= 100ms, availability 99.95% monthly.

SLI measurement and error budget:
- Measure latency at the gateway as primary SLI (inclusive of routing and pre/post-processing).
- Error budget policy: when error budget burned > 50% in 7 days -> reduce risky rollouts and enable stricter canaries.

Perf testing:
- Use bench-suite (eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite) with representative workloads and p95 targets.
- Load tests performed on staging with traffic shaping and production-like model artifacts.

7) ADRs (Architecture Decision Records)
------------------------------------
Process:
- Create an ADR for any decision that affects cross-team behavior, public API, infra topology, or data residency.
- Template: title, status (proposed|accepted|deprecated), context, decision, consequences, alternatives considered, date, authors, reviewers.
- Store ADRs in the repo at docs/adrs/ and reference the confluence page.

Representative ADRs:
- ADR-2025-09: Tokenization compatibility and model versioning policy (accepted).
- ADR-2025-12: Edge routing with smart-fallbacks (accepted).
- ADR-2026-01: Standardizing quantization profile naming (accepted).

8) Change & Rollout Process
--------------------------
- All changes to standards follow this flow: proposal (PR + ADR) -> review by standards working group -> acceptance -> update confluence doc -> 2-week grace period for team adoption -> enforcement via CI checks.
- Exceptions require documented approval (email + review) and must include a rollback plan.

Appendices
---------
A. Example OpenAPI snippet:

paths:
  /v1/engines/{engine_id}/completions:
    post:
      summary: Create completion
      requestBody:
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: object
              properties:
                model_id:
                  type: string
                input:
                  type: string
                max_tokens:
                  type: integer
      responses:
        200:
          description: successful completion

B. ADR template (text):
- title: short
- status: proposed/accepted/deprecated
- context: problem statement and background
- decision: chosen approach
- consequences: operational and technical impact
- alternatives: considered and rejected
- date, authors, reviewers

C. Pre-merge CI checklist (copyable):
- [ ] OpenAPI spec validated
- [ ] Linter and unit tests pass
- [ ] Integration / contract tests included
- [ ] Performance regression run for affected services
- [ ] ADR created if cross-team impact

Owners & Governance
-------------------
- Standards WG: eng-architecture (rotating chairs: Avery Chen, Maya Patel).
- Primary owners by area: API (API Platform), Runtime & Model Serving (Eng Serving Runtime), Observability (Eng Platform + SRE).
- Review cadence: quarterly review of standards; emergency patches as-needed.

Contact & Resources
-------------------
- Slack channels: #standards, #eng-architecture, #model-serving
- Docs repo: git@repo.redwood:docs/architecture
- Related confluence pages: architecture-standards-principles-and-adrs-2026-03-04.json, runtime-architecture

This document is intended as a living standard. Please open a PR or an ADR to propose changes.
